phase: P4 — DESIGN ONLY. The generator has NOT been run; nothing under islamic-banking-services was touched.
note: Per DESIGN.md §8 this fragment is DATA. The 8 service domains below carry no hand-written service code: one template upgrade turns each entry into api/openapi.yaml, a Flyway migration, a repository, a rules component with generated tests, api/events.yaml and authorization deny-tests. The 9th governance domain must cost one entry in this file.

conventions.money: Every field of type 'money' generates THREE columns — <name>_minor BIGINT NOT NULL (signed), <name>_currency CHAR(3) NOT NULL (ISO 4217 alpha), <name>_exponent SMALLINT NOT NULL — and an OpenAPI object {amountMinor:int64, currency:^[A-Z]{3}$, exponent:int32}. The exponent comes from ONE shared ISO 4217 table in the generated parent (BHD/KWD/OMR/TND = 3, JPY = 0, USD/EUR = 2). A hardcoded x100 is a bug. No float, no double, no BigDecimal-from-string anywhere in a money path.
conventions.ratio: Every field of type 'ratio' generates TWO columns — <name>_num BIGINT NOT NULL, <name>_den BIGINT NOT NULL CHECK (<name>_den > 0) — and an OpenAPI object {numerator:int64, denominator:int64}. A ratio is never rendered as a decimal on the wire. Arithmetic is integer multiply-then-divide with the record's recorded roundingPolicy; comparison and summation of ratios use a common denominator, never a quotient.

typeMapping.enum: TEXT + CHECK (col IN (...)) / type: string enum: [...]
typeMapping.digest: CHAR(64) + CHECK (col ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') / type: string pattern ^[0-9a-f]{64}$ — SHA-256 hex

conventions.controlRecordShape: controlRecord.fields is the ONLY place a field is defined. controlRecord.identifiers names which of those fields are identifiers and of what kind. controlRecord.money names which are money. controlRecord.ratios names which are ratios and their integer constraint. No field is defined twice.
conventions.behaviourQualifier: Each BQ generates a child table (<cr_table>_<bq_slug>, FK to the control record, ON DELETE RESTRICT because §5.8 is append-only), a sub-resource /v1/{crSlug}/{crId}/{bqSlug}, and one operation per actionTerm. cardinality 'one' generates a singleton sub-resource (UNIQUE on the FK); 'many' generates a collection.
conventions.ruleExpressionLanguage: A restricted, generable subset. Terms: field paths (cr.field, bq.Name[].field), literals, money/ratio accessors (.minor, .currency, .num, .den). Operators: == != < <= > >= && || ! implies, in / not in, is null / is not null. Functions: sum(path), count(path), exists(path where expr), round(expr, policy), effectiveAt(ref, date), status(ref). Nothing else — an assertion that needs more than this is not in the catalog, it is in notDerivable.
conventions.onViolation: reject = HTTP 422 with a generated problem+json carrying the rule id, and NO state change. flag = the write succeeds and an append-only finding row plus the rule's event are emitted. Exactly these two values, per DESIGN.md §8.
conventions.ruleScope: scope 'local' is decidable from this service's own rows and generates a real assertion. scope 'cross-domain' needs another service's state: the template generates a PolicyPort interface, a generated client from the named dependency's contract, a deny-by-default stub, and a contract test — and until the port is wired the rule DEGRADES TO flag and the degradation is itself recorded on the record (policyPortWired=false). A cross-domain rule silently passing is the failure mode this names.
conventions.testVectors: Optional per rule. Each vector is {name, given, expect} and generates one JUnit parameterised case. Money and ratio rules carry a 3-decimal (BHD/KWD/OMR/TND), a 0-decimal (JPY) and a 2-decimal (USD) vector, because that is where an exponent bug hides.
conventions.appendOnly: Every domain in this area is governance evidence. The generated repository exposes no DELETE and no in-place UPDATE of a decided/issued/computed row; a correction is a new row that supersedes the old one. DESIGN.md §5.8.
conventions.shariahReviewed: Every 'shariah' block in this fragment carries reviewed:false and the literal string 'UNREVIEWED — requires named Shariah board sign-off'. The generator stamps that string into the OpenAPI description of every Shariah-bearing schema and into the repo README. It is removed only by a named SSB, never by a developer.

notDerivable: Hijri/Gregorian calendar conversion. The catalog records calendarBasis, hawlStartsOn, hawlEndsOn and hawlDays as data; converting between calendars (and the 354-vs-355-day lunar year) is a library dependency, not a generated artifact. The generator must NOT emit arithmetic that assumes a fixed lunar year length.

Metal spot prices, index constituents and issuer revenue disclosures. These are external feeds. The catalog records the value with its source and asOf; it never generates a fetcher and never defaults a price.
The ISO 4217 exponent table and the money conversion function. ONE shared implementation in the generated parent (DESIGN.md §6), not 8 copies.

Any authoritative cross-domain join (was this SSB mandate ACTIVE on the fatwa's issuance date; is this ruling ISSUED and effective over this period). Generable only as a PolicyPort + generated client + deny-by-default stub; see conventions.ruleScope.
Free-text Shariah reasoning (decisionBasis, scope, customerVisibleReason, managementResponse). Stored and digested, never validated or inferred by generated code.

The choice of rounding policy, zakat base method, purification formula, nisab metal and mass, and whether an administrative (Amilin) deduction is permitted. Each is a required recorded field with a ruling reference and NO default. A default here would be a compliance claim the code cannot back.
Beneficiary (asnaf) eligibility determination, SNC classification, and whether a contract is void. The generated code records, quarantines and routes; it never decides.

A 'halal', 'compliant' or 'shariahApproved' boolean. No domain in this fragment has one, by design. The strongest statement the estate may make is: this decision applied criterion <id> of policy <id> version <n>, approved by ruling <id>, with evidenceQuality <q>.

cr.status in ['TERMINATED','EXPIRED'] implies cr.terminationReason is not null
cr.supersedesMandateId is null || status(cr.supersedesMandateId) in ['TERMINATED','EXPIRED']
rules.rationale: A renewal is a new row; the superseded row must already be closed, so two ACTIVE mandates can never overlap for the same seat.

rules.assert: no in-place update of mandateId, memberPartyId, boardId, termStartsOn, termEndsOn or appointmentReference once cr.status != 'NOMINATED'

fields.description: True where effectiveFrom precedes issuedOn — which happens on Shariah non-compliance remediation. Requires a justification rather than being silently allowed.

fields.description: METHOD_SELECTION and POLICY_PARAMETER are what let Income Purification and Zakat Calculation point at an authority instead of hardcoding a formula.

fields.name: basisSchoolNote
fields.description: Free text, deliberately NOT an enum of madhhabs. Attributing a ruling to a school of law is a scholarly claim this code must not encode as a closed list.

fields.name: jurisdiction
fields.description: Null means not jurisdiction-scoped.

fields.name: documentDigest
fields.description: SHA-256 of the signed ruling document. This is what makes the repository evidence rather than a note.

fields.description: False means the citation came from a secondary source. This is the field that stops the estate laundering commentary into authority.

rules.assert: cr.status == 'ISSUED' implies count(RulingSignatory where position == 'CONCUR') >= 1
rules.rationale: A ruling with no concurring signatory is not a ruling. AAOIFI GS 18.

rules.assert: all RulingSignatory: effectiveAt(mandateId, cr.issuedOn) == 'ACTIVE'
rules.rationale: Every signatory must have held an ACTIVE mandate on the issuance date. Needs the directory's state, so it generates a PolicyPort; while unwired it flags and policyPortWired records that it did.

rules.assert: cr.retroactive == (cr.effectiveFrom < cr.issuedOn) && (cr.retroactive implies cr.retroactiveJustification is not null)
rules.rationale: Retroactive effect is real in remediation but must be declared and justified, never inferred from the dates.

rules.assert: no in-place update of documentDigest, documentUri, issuedOn, resolutionNumber or decisionBasis once cr.status == 'ISSUED'
rules.rationale: An ISSUED ruling is immutable. A change is a new ruling that supersedes it, plus an Amendment History row carrying the prior digest. DESIGN.md §5.8.

rules.assert: cr.status == 'SUPERSEDED' implies (cr.supersededByRulingId is not null && cr.effectiveTo is not null)
cr.supersedesRulingId is null || status(cr.supersedesRulingId) == 'SUPERSEDED'
rules.rationale: Supersession is a closed two-sided link, so 'which ruling governs date D' has exactly one answer.

rules.assert: cr.status == 'WITHDRAWN' implies cr.withdrawalReason is not null
cr.rulingType in ['SCREENING_CRITERIA','POLICY_PARAMETER','METHOD_SELECTION'] implies count(CitedStandard) >= 1
rules.rationale: A ruling that sets a screening criterion, a policy parameter or a computation method with no cited standard is unsourced. It is recorded and flagged rather than rejected — an SSB may rule on its own authority — but it never passes silently.

rules.assert: all CitedStandard: (body in ['AAOIFI','IFSB'] implies (standardCode is not null && clause is not null))
rules.rationale: A bare 'per AAOIFI' is not a citation. Code and clause or nothing.

rules.assert: count(CitedStandard where primaryTextObtained == false) == 0
rules.rationale: Secondary-source citations are permitted and labelled. The flag is the label.

rules.assert: cr.dissentRecorded == (count(RulingSignatory where position == 'DISSENT') > 0)
rules.rationale: The dissent flag must match the signatory rows; a hidden dissent is the one thing a ruling repository must not be able to do.

rules.assert: count(ConditionOfApproval where mandatory == true && status == 'BREACHED') == 0

serviceDomains.name: Shariah Compliance Review
serviceDomains.gateHonesty: THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL COMPONENT IN THE ESTATE, AND THE EASIEST TO OVERSTATE. Transaction-level Shariah screening is a regulatory requirement in exactly ONE jurisdiction for ONE product: Bangladesh Bank IBRPD Circular No. 01 of 27 September 2026, 'Guidelines on Islamic Credit Card Operations of Banks'. Everywhere else — including the Malaysian MCC blocking practised by Maybank Islamic Ikhwan, AmBank Islamic and Bank Islam Card-i — it is ISSUER PRACTICE, not regulation. That fact is not a README footnote here: it is the mandateBasis enum on every screening policy, it is enforced by rule ISB-GOV-SCR-02, and a gate running in ENFORCING mode without a recorded basis is rejected. The rule set itself is DATA (ScreeningPolicy + ScreeningCriterion rows, per jurisdiction, per product scope, effective-dated, each approved by a rulingId). There is no screening logic in code — the generated rules component evaluates rows and cannot evaluate anything else.

fields.name: productScope
fields.description: e.g. ISLAMIC_CREDIT_CARD. Carried because the only regulation that mandates transaction screening mandates it for one product.

fields.name: policyVersion
fields.description: Monotonic. Recorded on the decision so the decision is replayable against the exact rule set that produced it.

fields.name: gateMode
fields.description: Per-jurisdiction, per-product. DISABLED still writes a case with decision NOT_APPLICABLE — a silent gate is worse than an absent one.

fields.name: mandateBasis
fields.description: Why this gate is running at all. REGULATION is correct for BD/ISLAMIC_CREDIT_CARD and, on the evidence behind this design, for nothing else.

fields.name: mandateBasisReference
fields.description: Required when mandateBasis == REGULATION. e.g. 'Bangladesh Bank IBRPD Circular No. 01, 27 Sep 2026, s.45 Bank Company Act 1991'.

fields.name: decision
fields.description: Exactly three outcomes plus the disabled case. There is no 'HALAL' value and there never will be.

fields.name: decisionReasonCode
fields.description: Names the criterionId that fired, or the policy's declared defaultOutcome. Never free text.

fields.name: appliedByRulingId
fields.description: The SSB ruling behind the criterion. Mandatory for a BLOCK.

fields.name: evidenceQuality
fields.description: An MCC or an ISO 20022 purpose code is a PROXY: a supermarket selling alcohol carries one code, and purpose codes are customer-supplied and absent on most domestic rails. The estate may never present a PROXY match as a determination.

fields.name: customerVisibleReason
fields.description: Required for a BLOCK. Blocking a payment on religious grounds without a reason the customer can see is itself a consumer-protection problem.

fields.name: supersedesCaseId
fields.description: A changed outcome is a new case. Decisions are never edited.

fields.name: interactionId
fields.description: x-fapi-interaction-id, correlation only. Never trusted as identity (DESIGN.md §5.6).

identifiers.note: FK to the ScreeningPolicy BQ row of the owning policy case.

fields.name: defaultOutcome
fields.description: Deny-by-default is CONFIGURABLE, not assumed. A deployment that defaults to BLOCK in a jurisdiction where screening is not required will break legitimate payments.

fields.name: selectorType
fields.description: MCC is ISO 18245; ISO20022_PURPOSE is the 4-character Purpose / ExtendedPurpose element. Both are proxies by construction — see rule ISB-GOV-SCR-04.

fields.name: inputHashed
fields.description: Counterparty identifiers are hashed before they reach the trace; the flag says which form the row holds, so a replay knows what it can and cannot re-derive.

fields.name: recognisedAsIncome
fields.description: Must be false. Present as a field so the invariant is assertable and auditable rather than implicit.

fields.name: checkCode
fields.description: AAOIFI SS 8 §3/2 (possession and risk transfer before onward sale), SS 3 §2/5/3 (set-off currency), SS 13 §9/6 (nothing charged to the IAH pool), SS 47 §5 (no accrual on arrears), SS 8 §4/3 and SS 47 §9 (fixed total price disclosed), SS 3 §2/1/4 and §2/1/8 (recovery costs and charity undertaking as separate non-income lines).

rules.assert: cr.decision == 'BLOCK' implies (cr.appliedByRulingId is not null && cr.customerVisibleReason is not null)
rules.rationale: The estate may never block a payment on religious grounds without a recorded, SSB-approved rule AND a reason the customer can read.

testVectors.name: block without ruling is refused
testVectors.given: decision=BLOCK, appliedByRulingId=null, customerVisibleReason='Merchant category not permitted'

testVectors.name: block without customer reason is refused

rules.assert: cr.gateMode == 'ENFORCING' implies (cr.mandateBasis in ['REGULATION','ISSUER_PRACTICE'] && (cr.mandateBasis == 'REGULATION' implies cr.mandateBasisReference is not null))
rules.rationale: This is the one-jurisdiction fact made executable. An enforcing gate must name why it enforces. On the evidence behind this design, only BD + ISLAMIC_CREDIT_CARD can honestly answer REGULATION.

testVectors.name: BD islamic credit card enforces on regulation
testVectors.given: jurisdiction=BD, productScope=ISLAMIC_CREDIT_CARD, gateMode=ENFORCING, mandateBasis=REGULATION, mandateBasisReference='Bangladesh Bank IBRPD Circular No. 01, 27 Sep 2026'

testVectors.name: enforcing with NOT_REQUIRED basis is refused
MY issuer practice may enforce without a regulation reference

rules.assert: exists(ScreeningPolicy where policyId == cr.policyId && version == cr.policyVersion && status == 'ACTIVE' && effectiveFrom <= cr.decidedAt && (effectiveTo is null || effectiveTo > cr.decidedAt))
rules.rationale: No decision may exist without the exact policy version that produced it being present and effective at decision time. This is what makes the rule set DATA: a decision the code could have reached without a row is refused.

rules.assert: all ScreeningCriterion: (selectorType in ['MCC','ISO20022_PURPOSE','MERCHANT_NAME_PATTERN'] implies evidenceQuality != 'DIRECT')
rules.rationale: An MCC or a purpose code is a coarse proxy — one code per mixed merchant, customer-supplied, absent on most domestic rails. Recording such a match as DIRECT evidence would turn a proxy into a determination.

rules.assert: cr.firedCriterionId is not null || cr.decisionReasonCode == concat('POLICY_DEFAULT:', cr.policyId)
rules.rationale: Every decision names the criterion that fired or the policy default. There is no third source of a decision, and in particular no code path.

rules.assert: cr.decision == 'REFER' implies count(Referral) >= 1
count(Referral where outcome is null && slaDueAt < now()) == 0
rules.rationale: An unresolved referral past SLA is an operational signal, not a reason to refuse the write.

rules.assert: cr.gateMode == 'DISABLED' implies cr.decision == 'NOT_APPLICABLE'
rules.rationale: A disabled gate still writes a case. The alternative — no row at all — makes 'was screening on' unanswerable after the fact.

rules.assert: all NonComplianceEvent: recognisedAsIncome == false
rules.rationale: Shariah non-compliant income never enters P&L. AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 and GS 9.

rules.assert: all NonComplianceEvent: (quarantinedAmount is null || (fundingAccountContractType not in ['Mudarabah','Musharakah','Wakala'] && segregatedLiabilityAccountRef is not null))
rules.rationale: Quarantined SNC income sits in a segregated liability and is never funded from an investment-account-holder pool. AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6: the Mudarib may not make a gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds.

rules.assert: all NonComplianceEvent: (charityChannelledAmount is null || (charityChannelledAmount.currency == quarantinedAmount.currency && charityChannelledAmount.minor <= quarantinedAmount.minor && charityChannelledAmount.minor >= 0))
rules.rationale: Integer minor units, one currency, never more channelled than quarantined.

rules.assert: all NonComplianceEvent: (determination != 'PENDING' implies (determinedByRulingId is not null && determinedAt is not null))
rules.rationale: The service records and routes; the SSB determines. A determination with no ruling behind it is the code pretending to be a scholar.

rules.assert: no in-place update of decision, decisionReasonCode, firedCriterionId, policyVersion, criteriaListVersion, decidedAt or evidenceQuality once the case row exists
rules.rationale: A changed outcome is a new case with supersedesCaseId set. DESIGN.md §5.8 — append-only for every Shariah non-compliance finding.

rules.assert: cr.supersedesCaseId is null || status(cr.supersedesCaseId) is not null
cr.appliedByRulingId is null || effectiveAt(cr.appliedByRulingId, cr.decidedAt) == 'ISSUED'
rules.rationale: A decision may not cite a withdrawn or not-yet-effective ruling. Needs the repository's state; degrades to flag while the PolicyPort is unwired.

rules.assert: all ContractIntegrityCheck: (citedStandardCode is not null && citedClause is not null)
rules.rationale: A contract-integrity check with no clause behind it is an opinion in a boolean.

rules.assert: all ScreeningCriterion: (outcome == 'BLOCK' implies (approvedByRulingId is not null && customerVisibleReason is not null))
rules.rationale: The BLOCK requirement is enforced where the criterion is authored, not only where it fires.

rules.assert: count(ScreeningCriterion group by policyId, precedence having count > 1) == 0
rules.rationale: Ambiguous precedence makes a decision non-replayable.

fields.name: impermissibleRatio

fields.name: capitalGainsIncluded

fields.name: recognisedAsIncome

ratios.note: Exact integer pair. Never a percentage, never a float.

serviceDomains.name: Zakat Calculation
serviceDomains.arithmetic:
EXACT INTEGER ONLY, four steps, each reproducible from the stored row:
  1. nisabValueMinor   = round(metalSpotPrice.minor * nisabMassMilligrams / spotPriceMassBasisMilligrams, roundingPolicy)
  2. netZakatableMinor = zakatableBaseAmount.minor - deductibleLiabilitiesAmount.minor
  3. nisabMet          = netZakatableMinor >= nisabValueMinor
  4. zakatDueMinor     = nisabMet ? round(netZakatableMinor * zakatRate.num / zakatRate.den, roundingPolicy) : 0
The rate is an EXACT ratio: 1/40 on a lunar (Hijri) basis. The often-quoted solar figure of ~2.577% is exactly 1/40 * 365/354 = 365/14160, so it too is an exact ratio and is stored as one — a float here would quietly change a religious due. Masses are int64 MILLIGRAMS (595 g = 595000 mg), so no decimal mass ever appears.

fields.name: baseMethod
fields.description: AAOIFI FAS 9 permitted both. FAS 39 'Financial reporting for Zakah' (from exposure draft F5/2019 v5.1, 8 July 2020) records that the Shariah standard only provided net assets and DROPS net invested funds. NET_INVESTED_FUNDS therefore needs a ruling and a legacy note.

fields.name: calendarBasis
fields.description: The obligation remains attached to the Hijri calendar; a solar basis is a reporting convenience that changes the rate.

fields.name: hawlDays
fields.description: 354 for a full lunar year per AAOIFI SS 35 as cited by ZATCA. A lunar year is 354 or 355 days in practice, so this is recorded, checked loosely and flagged — never silently normalised.

fields.name: zakatRate
fields.description: Exact. 1/40 on HIJRI_LUNAR; 365/14160 on GREGORIAN_SOLAR (= 1/40 * 365/354). Never 0.025 and never 2.5.

fields.name: zakatRateRulingId
fields.description: Required only to override the standard rate for the recorded calendar basis.

fields.name: nisabMassMilligrams
fields.description: Integer milligrams. 595 g silver = 595000. The gold figure diverges across sources (85 g against 87.48 g) and the silver figure across sources too (595 g against 612.36 g); only the silver 595 g is traceable to a primary citation, so this is a SOURCED PARAMETER, never a constant in code.

fields.name: spotPriceMassBasisMilligrams
fields.description: What mass metalSpotPrice is the price OF (e.g. 1000000 for a price per kilogram). Makes step 1 a pure integer ratio.

fields.name: roundingPolicy
fields.description: Required, no default.

fields.name: payerRole
fields.description: Required. The research is explicit: state plainly whether the bank pays on the customer's behalf or only informs. An assessment that does not say is a misleading document.

fields.name: advisoryOnly
fields.description: True for a customer assessment presented as a computation with visible inputs rather than as a determination of the customer's religious obligation.

money.note: Price of spotPriceMassBasisMilligrams of the metal. int64 minor units.
Derived. May be negative; signed int64 is required.
Derived. Zero when nisab is not met.

fields.name: inclusionRatio
fields.description: Exact. 1/1 for fully zakatable, 0/1 for excluded, and a partial ratio where the SSB rules one applies.

fields.name: divergenceNote
fields.description: e.g. 'Gold nisab is quoted as 85 g and as 87.48 g; silver as 595 g and as 612.36 g. Only silver 595 g (200 dirhams, AAOIFI SS 35 p.874 as cited by ZATCA) is traceable to a primary citation here.'

fields.name: methodStated
fields.description: The certificate must carry the method, the nisab source, the spot price and its asOf. A bare number is not usable for religious compliance and is not defensible.

rules.assert: (cr.calendarBasis == 'HIJRI_LUNAR' implies (cr.zakatRate.num * 40 == cr.zakatRate.den || cr.zakatRateRulingId is not null)) && (cr.calendarBasis == 'GREGORIAN_SOLAR' implies (cr.zakatRate.num * 14160 == cr.zakatRate.den * 365 || cr.zakatRateRulingId is not null))
rules.rationale: Cross-multiplied so the check is exact integer equality with no division. 1/40 lunar, 365/14160 solar; any other rate needs a ruling.

testVectors.name: lunar 2.577 percent without a ruling refused

rules.assert: cr.nisabValue.minor == round(cr.metalSpotPrice.minor * cr.nisabMassMilligrams / cr.spotPriceMassBasisMilligrams, cr.roundingPolicy) && cr.nisabValue.currency == cr.metalSpotPrice.currency

testVectors.name: silver 595 g at BHD 850.000 per kg

cr.nisabMet == (cr.netZakatableAmount.minor >= cr.nisabValue.minor) && cr.nisabValue.currency == cr.netZakatableAmount.currency
rules.rationale: A nisab comparison across two currencies is the bug that silently makes everyone liable or nobody.

rules.assert: cr.zakatDueAmount.minor == (cr.nisabMet ? round(cr.netZakatableAmount.minor * cr.zakatRate.num / cr.zakatRate.den, cr.roundingPolicy) : 0)

rules.assert: cr.nisabMassSourceRef is not null && cr.metalSpotPriceSource is not null && cr.metalSpotPriceAsOf is not null && count(NisabReference) == 1
rules.rationale: A nisab with no source and no asOf is a constant someone typed. The divergence across published figures (85 g against 87.48 g gold; 595 g against 612.36 g silver) is exactly why this is refused rather than defaulted.

rules.assert: cr.baseMethod == 'NET_INVESTED_FUNDS' implies (cr.legacyBasisNote is not null && cr.baseMethodRulingId is not null)
rules.rationale: FAS 39 drops the net-invested-funds method. Using it is a deliberate legacy choice that must name its authority.

rules.rationale: A certificate that does not say whether the bank paid or merely informed, and on what method, is a misleading document.

rules.assert: all ZakatableAssetLine: (inclusionRatio.den > 0 && inclusionRatio.num >= 0 && inclusionRatio.num <= inclusionRatio.den && includedAmount.minor == round(grossAmount.minor * inclusionRatio.num / inclusionRatio.den, cr.roundingPolicy) && includedAmount.currency == grossAmount.currency)
cr.zakatableBaseAmount.minor == sum(ZakatableAssetLine.includedAmount) && cr.deductibleLiabilitiesAmount.minor == sum(DeductibleLiabilityLine.amount)
rules.rationale: The base must be the sum of its visible lines. The research is explicit that a zakat API should expose the method and the inputs, not a single opaque number.

rules.assert: cr.hawlEndsOn > cr.hawlStartsOn && (cr.calendarBasis == 'HIJRI_LUNAR' implies cr.hawlDays in [354, 355])
rules.rationale: A lunar year is 354 or 355 days. Flagged, not rejected, and the Hijri conversion itself is NOT generated — see notDerivable.

rules.rationale: Zakat requires stable ownership above nisab for a full hawl. A dip below is recorded and flagged; whether it breaks the hawl is an SSB question, not this service's.

rules.assert: no in-place update of any money field, zakatRate, nisabMassMilligrams, metalSpotPrice, baseMethod, roundingPolicy or calendarBasis once cr.status in ['COMPUTED','CERTIFIED']
rules.rationale: A revision is a new assessment with supersedesAssessmentId. A certificate already in a customer's hands must stay reproducible. DESIGN.md §5.8.

rules.assert: effectiveAt(cr.baseMethodRulingId, cr.hawlEndsOn) == 'ISSUED'
cr.advisoryOnly == true || cr.subjectType == 'INSTITUTION'
rules.rationale: A customer-facing assessment presented as a determination rather than an advisory computation is the one output of this domain most likely to be read as a religious ruling.

serviceDomains.name: Zakat Distribution
serviceDomains.arithmetic: EXACT INTEGER CONSERVATION. Every minor unit that enters the fund leaves it as an allocation, an administrative deduction or a declared residual — nothing is lost to rounding silently. Allocation weights are exact ratios summed over a common denominator (sum(num_i * L / den_i) == L where L = lcm of the denominators), never floats summed to 0.9999.

fields.name: sourceAssessmentId

fields.name: currency
fields.description: A distribution run is single-currency. Cross-currency is two runs, because converting a religious due needs a recorded rate and a ruling.

fields.name: residualAmount
fields.description: Explicit. Every unit lost to rounding lands here; it is never absorbed into the last allocation.

fields.name: remittedToAuthority
fields.description: Several jurisdictions require remittance to a national zakat authority rather than direct distribution. Where true, the beneficiary allocation is the authority's responsibility, not this service's.

fields.name: segregatedAccountContractType
fields.description: Zakat funds are held, not invested. An investment-account contract type here is refused by ISB-GOV-ZDS-05.

fields.name: asnafCategory
fields.description: The eight classical categories of Qur'an 9:60. No AAOIFI or IFSB clause for this list was obtained in the research behind this design — see uncertain. Eligibility against a category is NEVER determined by this service.

fields.name: weight
fields.description: Exact. Weights sum to exactly 1 over a common denominator.

fields.name: permitted
fields.description: Whether the institution may take an Amilin (collector's) share of the funds it administers. A live scholarly and jurisdictional question, so it is a recorded decision with a ruling, never a default.

rules.assert: cr.totalAvailableAmount.minor == sum(BeneficiaryAllocation.allocatedAmount) + AdministrativeDeduction.amount.minor + cr.residualAmount.minor
rules.rationale: The conservation rule. Every minor unit is accounted for, including the rounding residue, which is why residualAmount is a field rather than a comment.

testVectors.name: BHD 3-decimal three-way split with residue
testVectors.given: totalAvailableAmount={minor:1000,currency:BHD,exponent:3}, three allocations of weight 1/3 at ROUND_DOWN giving 333 each, AdministrativeDeduction.amount.minor=0
testVectors.expect: residualAmount.minor == 1 and the run is accepted

testVectors.name: JPY 0-decimal run that loses a unit is refused

rules.assert: cr.allocationBasis == 'ASNAF_CATEGORY_WEIGHTS' implies sum_exact_ratio(BeneficiaryAllocation.weight) == 1
rules.rationale: Summed over a common denominator in integers. Floats summing to 0.99999999 is the bug this rule exists for.

testVectors.name: three thirds as 0.33 each is refused

rules.assert: all BeneficiaryAllocation: (allocatedAmount.currency == cr.currency && allocatedAmount.minor >= 0 && sum(Disbursement.amount where allocationId == allocationId) <= allocatedAmount.minor)
all FundInflow: amount.currency == cr.currency && all Disbursement: amount.currency == cr.currency && cr.totalAvailableAmount.currency == cr.currency
rules.rationale: One currency per run. Converting zakat needs a recorded rate and a ruling, so it is a separate run, not an implicit conversion.

rules.assert: cr.segregatedAccountRef is not null && cr.segregatedAccountContractType in ['Wadiah','QardHassan','SEGREGATED_LIABILITY','TRUST_ACCOUNT']
rules.rationale: Zakat funds are segregated and not commingled with the institution's own income or with an investment-account-holder pool. AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6 forbids charitable disbursement out of Mudarabah funds.

rules.assert: (AdministrativeDeduction.permitted == false implies AdministrativeDeduction.amount.minor == 0) && (AdministrativeDeduction.permitted == true implies AdministrativeDeduction.rulingId is not null) && (AdministrativeDeduction.cap is null || AdministrativeDeduction.basis.num * AdministrativeDeduction.cap.den <= AdministrativeDeduction.cap.num * AdministrativeDeduction.basis.den)
rules.rationale: An institution taking a cut of zakat it administers needs a named ruling and must stay inside the recorded cap. The cap comparison is cross-multiplied so it is exact integer arithmetic.

rules.assert: count(BeneficiaryAllocation where asnafCategory == 'AMILIN' && beneficiaryRef == cr.fundPoolId) == 0 || AdministrativeDeduction.rulingId is not null
rules.rationale: Allocating to AMILIN where the beneficiary is the administering institution itself is the administrative deduction wearing a different hat. It needs the same ruling.

rules.assert: cr.totalDisbursedAmount.minor == sum(Disbursement.amount where status in ['SENT','SETTLED']) - sum(ReturnedFunds.amount)
cr.status == 'COMPLETED' implies (cr.totalDisbursedAmount.minor + cr.residualAmount.minor + AdministrativeDeduction.amount.minor == cr.totalAvailableAmount.minor)
rules.rationale: A completed run reconciles to the minor unit or it is not completed.

rules.assert: cr.remittedToAuthority implies (cr.zakatAuthorityId is not null && cr.allocationBasis == 'REMITTED_TO_AUTHORITY' && count(BeneficiaryAllocation where beneficiaryType != 'AUTHORITY') == 0)
rules.rationale: Where funds go to a national zakat authority, this service must not also pretend to have chosen beneficiaries.

rules.assert: all BeneficiaryAllocation: (beneficiaryType == 'INDIVIDUAL' implies (eligibilityVerifiedOn is not null && eligibilityVerifiedByOrgan is not null))
rules.rationale: Eligibility is verified by a person or an authority, never derived by this service. The flag records the gap rather than inventing a determination.

rules.assert: no in-place update of any money field, weight, asnafCategory or allocationBasis once cr.status != 'PLANNED'; no DELETE of a FundInflow, BeneficiaryAllocation, Disbursement or ReturnedFunds row
rules.rationale: DESIGN.md §5.8.

rules.assert: all FundInflow: (sourceAssessmentId is null || status(sourceAssessmentId) in ['COMPUTED','CERTIFIED'])
no FundInflow or Disbursement references a charity pool managed by isb-sadaqah-and-charity-management
rules.rationale: Zakat and sadaqah/purification/SNC charity funds are different funds with different permitted uses. Commingling them is the mistake a shared 'charity' table would make inevitable.

serviceDomains.name: Sadaqah And Charity Management
serviceDomains.designNote: THIS POOL IS NOT ONE POOL. It receives late-payment charity (AAOIFI SS 3 §2/1/8), quarantined Shariah non-compliant income, income-purification proceeds and voluntary sadaqah — and the permitted USE of each differs by its SOURCE. Every inflow is therefore source-tagged, a PermittedUsePolicy row says what each source may fund, and no outflow may draw more from a source bucket than that bucket received. Zakat is explicitly NOT here: it has its own fund, its own categories and its own service.

fields.name: currentBalance
fields.description: DERIVED from the append-only PoolBalanceMovement ledger. The generated repository exposes no setter; rule ISB-GOV-CHR-01 refuses a direct write.

fields.name: commingleWithZakat
fields.description: Must be false. Present as a field so the invariant is assertable instead of implicit.

money.note: Derived from the movement ledger, never written directly.

fields.name: sourceCategory
fields.description: Permitted use differs by source. This tag is what makes that enforceable.

fields.name: lateChargeKind
fields.description: AAOIFI SS 3 distinguishes recovery of actual costs (§2/1/4) from the debtor's charity undertaking (§2/1/8). Recovery of actual costs is NOT charity and must not arrive here.

fields.name: recognisedAsIncome
fields.description: Must be false.

fields.name: beneficiaryIsRelatedParty
fields.description: Charity flowing to a related party of the institution is the obvious abuse of a pool funded by penalties and non-compliant income.

fields.name: sequenceNumber
fields.description: Monotonic per pool. The ledger's order is data, not insertion luck.

rules.assert: cr.currentBalance.minor == cr.openingBalance.minor + sum(PoolBalanceMovement.amount where direction == 'IN') - sum(PoolBalanceMovement.amount where direction == 'OUT') && no direct write of cr.currentBalance
rules.rationale: The balance is a fold of an append-only ledger. A settable balance is how a charity pool quietly loses money.

rules.assert: all PoolBalanceMovement: (amount.currency == cr.currency && balanceAfter.currency == cr.currency) && all CharityInflow: amount.currency == cr.currency && all CharityOutflow: amount.currency == cr.currency
rules.rationale: One currency per pool. A cross-currency charity pool needs a recorded conversion and a ruling, so it is a second pool.

rules.assert: all CharityInflow: (recognisedAsIncome == false && (sourceCategory in ['LATE_PAYMENT_CHARITY','SNC_QUARANTINED_INCOME','INCOME_PURIFICATION'] implies originContractType not in ['Mudarabah','Musharakah','Wakala']))
rules.rationale: Charity, penalty and quarantined income never enter P&L, and are never funded from an investment-account-holder pool. AAOIFI SS 13 §9/6: the Mudarib may not make a loan, gift or charitable donation out of Mudarabah funds.

rules.assert: all CharityInflow: lateChargeKind != 'TAAWIDH_ACTUAL_LOSS'
rules.rationale: Ta'widh — recovery of the actual costs directly incurred (AAOIFI SS 3 §2/1/4) — is a cost recovery, not charity. Admitting it here would quietly convert a recoverable cost into a donation, or worse, a penalty into income.

rules.assert: all CharityOutflow: exists(PermittedUsePolicy where sourceCategory == sourceCategoryDrawn && purposeCode == purposeCode && permitted == true && effectiveFrom <= disbursedOn && (effectiveTo is null || effectiveTo >= disbursedOn))
rules.rationale: Permitted use is DATA, per source category, effective-dated, each row approved by a ruling. There is no hardcoded notion of what charity money may fund.

rules.assert: for each sourceCategory: sum(PoolBalanceMovement.amount where direction == 'OUT' && sourceCategory == c) <= sum(PoolBalanceMovement.amount where direction == 'IN' && sourceCategory == c)
rules.rationale: No borrowing across source buckets. Spending purification money on a purpose only permitted for voluntary sadaqah is exactly what a single undifferentiated balance would allow.

testVectors.name: cannot spend SNC bucket from the sadaqah bucket

rules.assert: cr.commingleWithZakat == false && count(CharityInflow where sourceServiceDomain == 'isb-zakat-distribution') == 0 && count(CharityInflow where sourceServiceDomain == 'isb-zakat-calculation') == 0
rules.rationale: Zakat has its own fund, its own eight categories and its own service. A zakat inflow arriving here is a routing bug with a religious consequence.

rules.assert: all CharityOutflow: (status in ['APPROVED','SENT','SETTLED'] implies (approvalRef is not null && approvedByOrgan == cr.disbursementApprovalOrgan))
count(CharityOutflow where beneficiaryIsRelatedParty == true) == 0
rules.rationale: A pool funded by penalties and non-compliant income paying a related party is the headline risk. Flagged and evented rather than rejected, because a legitimate related charitable foundation exists in some groups — but it is never silent.

rules.assert: all PoolBalanceMovement: ((direction == 'IN') == (inflowId is not null)) && ((direction == 'OUT') == (outflowId is not null)) && sequenceNumber is unique per pool and strictly increasing with occurredAt
rules.rationale: Every movement is traceable to exactly one inflow or outflow, and the ledger order is explicit rather than dependent on insertion order.

rules.assert: all Attestation: closingBalance.minor == openingBalance.minor + sum(PoolBalanceMovement.amount where occurredAt in [periodFrom, periodTo] && direction == 'IN') - sum(PoolBalanceMovement.amount where occurredAt in [periodFrom, periodTo] && direction == 'OUT')
rules.rationale: An attestation that does not reconcile against the ledger it attests to is worse than none.

rules.assert: no in-place update of amount, sourceCategory, direction, balanceAfter or sequenceNumber on any PoolBalanceMovement, CharityInflow or CharityOutflow row; no DELETE of any of them
rules.rationale: DESIGN.md §5.8. A correction is a reversing movement.

rules.assert: all PermittedUsePolicy: effectiveAt(approvedByRulingId, effectiveFrom) == 'ISSUED'
cr.status == 'CLOSED' implies (cr.currentBalance.minor == 0 && cr.closedOn is not null)
rules.rationale: A closed pool with money in it is money nobody owns.

uncertain: Whether a late-payment charity undertaking is permissible at all. AAOIFI SS 3 §2/1/8 permits it; stricter opinions reject it. The catalog records the undertaking and its ruling; it does not take a side. The gharamah-against-ta'widh distinction is modelled as lateChargeKind for exactly this reason.

Whether purification proceeds, SNC-quarantined income and voluntary sadaqah may share one pool. Modelled as one pool with hard per-source buckets and a per-source permitted-use matrix, so an SSB can split them later without a data migration. This is a design bet, not a ruling.
What charity money may actually fund. Entirely data (PermittedUsePolicy); the catalog ships no purpose codes at all.
Whether a related-party charitable foundation may receive these funds. Flagged, never decided.

Dormant and unclaimed balances. Included as a source category because they commonly end up in such a pool, but the treatment is jurisdictional (often an unclaimed-property regime rather than a Shariah question) and nothing here asserts it is charity.

IFSB-22's disclosure templates. Cited as the reporting target; the primary tables were not read (the IFSB standards pages are WAF-protected and several PDFs are scanned), so no reporting projection shape is specified in this entry.
